Let $X$ be a multiset with members drawn from the set $\W$.
We write $\mathbf{N}_X$ for the function which maps every $x\in\W$ to the natural number corresponding to the number of times that $x$ occurs in $X$.
We refer to $\mathbf{N}_X(x)$ as the _multiplicity_ of $x$ in $X$.

Let $X$ and $Y$ be any two multisets with members drawn from the set $\W$.

a. Formulate the statements $x\in X$ and $X\subset Y$ in terms of $\mathbf{N}_X$ and $\mathbf{N}_Y$.

b. Express the functions $\mathbf{N}_{X\cap Y}$, $\mathbf{N}_{X\cup Y}$, and $\mathbf{N}_{X-Y}$ in terms of $\mathbf{N}_X$ and $\mathbf{N}_Y$.

The union of two sets $X$ and $Y$ can be characterized as the smallest set containing both $X$ and $Y$.
This, however, is not so for the union of two multisets.
To see this, let $X\sqcup Y$ be the multiset $Z$ such that (i) $X\subset Z$ and $Y\subset Z$ and (ii) for any multiset $W$: if $X\subset W$ and $Y\subset W$, then $Z\subset W$.

c. Supply multisets $X$ and $Y$ for which $X\cup\Y\neq X\sqcup Y$.

d. Express the function $\mathbf{N}_{X\sqcup Y}$ in terms of $\mathbf{N}_X$ and $\mathbf{N}_Y$.

d. Show that, for any multisets $X$ and $Y$:
$$
(X \cup Y) - Y = X
$$
Under what conditions does the following equality hold:
$$
(X \sqcup Y) - Y = X
$$
